note.title: Tense recognition
note.overview: This note supports 4 source-backed questions on Tense recognition.
learningGoals: Identify the grammatical clue and apply it accurately.
mustMemoriseRules: perfect stem + eram, eras, erat, eramus, eratis, erant

workedExamples.why: perfect stem + eram, eras, erat, eramus, eratis, erant

commonMistakes: Recognising a stem but missing person, number or tense.
Recognising one familiar word without checking the complete grammatical clue.
detailedExplanation: This note supports 4 source-backed questions on Tense recognition.

A Latin verb form combines stem, tense information and a personal ending. Work from the ending inward: identify person and number, then tense or mood, then translate with the correct time relationship.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
